title: Serving Time
logline: A wealthy criminal bought their way out of a prison sentence by legally transferring the conviction to a desperate volunteer, who now wants out.

roles.description: Sold their freedom to pay off their family's debts; deeply regrets it.
Spoiled, cowardly, believes everything and everyone has a price tag.
Runs a brutal penal colony; doesn't care who serves the time as long as the cell is full.
An opulent, heavily secured legal office hovering above the squalor.
A high-security deep-space prison focused on hard labor.
A notoriously corrupt legal system that allows conviction trading.

public_situation: A high-profile {role:guilty_patrician} was publicly convicted of a horrific crime, but rumors say they are still seen drinking in high-end lounges.
private_truth: The patrician exploited a rare legal loophole to pay a desperate {role:fall_guy} to serve the twenty-year sentence in their place.

beats.public_change: The fall guy's family publicly protests, claiming they never received the promised payout.

missions.reason: Hires the pilot to quietly dock and pick up an official, sealed pardon document from a corrupt judge.
missions.private_fact: The patrician is only doing this because the fall guy threatened to expose the identity transfer.

missions.reason: The fall guy manages a smuggled comms link and begs the pilot to buy clean ID chips and officially dock at the colony to deliver them.
missions.private_fact: The fall guy plans to use the pardon and the new ID to completely disappear.

beats.public_change: The prison warden puts the facility on lockdown, suspecting outside interference.

missions.reason: The warden demands the pilot scan the colony's intake biometric logs from the exterior ports to prove no identity transfers occurred.
missions.private_fact: The warden actually facilitated the transfer and just wants to know if the pilot has proof.

beats.public_change: The lockdown lifts, and the pilot approaches the prison with the physical pardon.

missions.reason: The pilot must officially dock and deliver the physical pardon to the warden to release the prisoner.
missions.private_fact: The patrician contacts the pilot, offering triple the courier fee to return the pardon to them so they can destroy it and keep the fall guy silenced forever.

player_choice.prompt: The pilot holds the pardon. They can free the fall guy or sell the document back to the patrician.

options.label: Deliver the pardon to the warden
Return the pardon to the patrician

resolutions.summary: The fall guy is legally released and uses the clean IDs to disappear. The patrician is furious but legally untouchable.

consequences.public_summary: Someone smuggled a pardon in for a poor kid serving a rich man's sentence.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot exposes the transfer to the warden.
resolutions.summary: The public evidence forces the bureau to act. The patrician is arrested, and the fall guy is released, though deeply traumatized.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot returns the pardon to the patrician.
resolutions.summary: The patrician destroys the pardon. The fall guy is trapped in the colony for twenty years, and the patrician continues their lavish life.

loose_threads.detail: The warden's public disclosure forms show a massive charitable donation from an anonymous trust exactly one day after the transfer.
A dockworker mentions seeing the patrician's ship leaving the system on the exact night of the crime they supposedly committed.

radio_hooks: Protests continue outside {role:penal_colony} over alleged 'conviction trading'.
{role:justice_bureau} denies any systemic issues with identity verification protocols.

voice_direction.fall_guy: Monotone, defeated delivery. Never ends a sentence with an upward inflection.
voice_direction.guilty_patrician: Brisk, entitled rhythm. Uses expensive, antiquated slang.
voice_direction.prison_warden: Deep, booming pitch. Speaks slowly, treating every conversation like an interrogation.
